checks.command: manual editorial review of all 96 final votar cards with the authoritative form substituted
checks.evidence: All 96 ES/RU pairs were read in identity order. Contexts distinguish habitual, completed, future and counterfactual voting; subjects make person and number explicit, and the Russian translations preserve object, stance, time and result.

checks.command: authoritative votar forms and identity/options/source-embedded contract check
checks.evidence: 96/96 surface forms match authoritative Jehle data across 16 scopes and six slots; mood/tense metadata is exact; top-level data and scope/person/number order match the immutable baseline; every prompt has one blank and lemma suffix; every option set has four unique forms from the same scope with the answer once; source and embedded are byte-identical.

checks.command: editorial rare-register, counterfactual and future-perfect-subjunctive barrier for votar
checks.evidence: All six pretérito anterior cards explicitly identify chronicle, literary, parliamentary or legal narration; all twelve future subjunctive cards explicitly identify legal or old legal language; all six De haberlo sabido translations begin with explicit Если бы ... знал/знали wording; all six future-perfect-subjunctive Russian translations use если окажется, что plus a completed vote.

Immutable baseline contained wrong surface forms in 30 cards, duplicate options in 30, answer-count errors in 34, 141 off-scope option entries across 42 cards, and 85 invalid-union entries across 25 cards; metadata and blank errors were 0. Final focused contract has zero defects in all categories.
Repository-native strict validator accepted all 96 cards across the expected 16 scopes and six person/number slots.
All three focused Go packages passed against the final embedded votar artifact.
